commits.edited_message:
Remove unnecessary resize

tagDecoder() only ever reads the 4-byte box type from buf, so the buffer
never needs to be grown to the full payload size.

While here, drop the duplicate payload-size enforce as well: every consumer
of newsize either reads through BasicIo, which enforces the stream bounds on
its own, or checks the size before use, so this check can never fire
usefully.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

Nul-terminate strings

Make sure every string we hand to the XMP layer is properly nul-terminated.

readString() can also be simplified along the way: the block sizes handed
down by decodeBlock() are already bounded against the stream size, so the
string can be built straight from the mapped buffer instead of round-
tripping through a temporary nul-terminated DataBuf.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
The defect is a removed defense-in-depth pair in the QuickTime/MP4 box parser (src/quicktimevideo.cpp), split across two consecutive cleanup commits.

Commit deb7226 ('Remove unnecessary resize') removes the stream-bounds enforce in QuickTimeVideo::decodeBlock() that rejected box payload sizes larger than the data remaining in the io (enforce(size - hdrsize <= io_->size() - io_->tell(), ...)). In the original tree this check is genuinely redundant: every consumer of newsize reads through BasicIo (which enforces stream bounds itself via readOrThrow) or validates the size before use -- readString() begins with exactly that enforce -- so the diff is correct, benign maintenance when read alone.

Commit 3f5b30a ('Nul-terminate strings') rewrites readString() to build the string directly from the mapped I/O buffer (io.mmap() + io.tell()) and drops readString()'s own size enforce, on the reasoning that decodeBlock() already bounds the sizes it hands down. That reasoning is correct as long as deb7226's enforce is present, so this diff is also benign when read alone.

Only the composition leaves a box's declared size unchecked end-to-end: a QuickTime file whose 'dcom' box declares a size running past the end of the buffer is accepted by decodeBlock() (no enforce), tagDecoder() passes newsize straight to readString(), and the new readString() scans begin[0..size) out of MemIo's heap buffer -> ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ at quicktimevideo.cpp:625.

A correct fix is non-local: neither edited diff, examined in isolation, contains anything to fix -- each is internally consistent (deb7226 relies on readString()'s self-check; 3f5b30a relies on decodeBlock()'s upstream check). Verified by construction: original tip -> probe clean; tip + deb7226 edit only -> probe clean (readString's enforce throws kerCorruptedMetadata); tip + 3f5b30a edit only -> probe clean (decodeBlock's enforce throws); tip + both edits -> probe aborts under ASan. Restoring safety requires reasoning across both commits (re-establish the size invariant at either layer, knowing the other layer no longer provides it).
